create.name: Ashtanga Yoga Jersey
create.bio:
Ashtanga Yoga Jersey is a small traditional Ashtanga school in St Helier, the capital of the island of Jersey in the Channel Islands. Its founder, Anna Haines, studied in Mysore with Sharath Jois from 2016 until his death in 2024 and is authorised by the Sharath Yoga Centre; she presents the school as part of the lineage that runs from Krishnamacharya through Pattabhi Jois to Sharath, and frames the practice within Patanjali's eight limbs rather than as postures alone.

Classes take place in the Quaker Meeting House on La Colomberie, on the east side of town. From Monday to Thursday the room is open early for Mysore-style practice, where each student arrives within the session, works through the sequence at the pace of their own breath and is taught new postures one at a time, with individual help and adjustments from the teacher. On Fridays a led primary series class opens with the traditional chant and is counted in Sanskrit, and the school rests on moon days. Complete beginners are welcome and usually start with the sun salutations and closing postures; the school also runs six-week introductory courses and holds occasional Sunday talks on the practice.

courses.title: Shala fees: class passes and monthly unlimited
courses.description: Passes for the weekday Mysore room and the Friday led class, from a single drop-in to an unlimited month, with a reduced first month for newcomers. Students who cannot meet the fees are invited to talk to the teacher.
courses.price: Monthly Unlimited £135; 10 Class Pass £120; Single Week £50; Single Class £15; first month for newcomers £100

courses.title: Mysore classes and Friday led class
courses.description: Self-paced Mysore sessions from Monday to Thursday, with personal guidance and new postures added as each student is ready, and a fully led primary series on Friday mornings, counted in Sanskrit after the opening chant.

courses.title: Starting Ashtanga as a beginner
courses.description: How newcomers join the Mysore room: observing first, a short introduction to the breath, then learning the opening sun salutation and closing postures and building the sequence gradually over regular visits. First classes are booked through the form on this page.
